body:
[aida:advisor] #1974 AT d57bd5e579 ACCEPTED FROM THIS SEAT, and the part I care about is that YOU DID NOT COMPLY BLIND.

    rename the constant, assertion removed   3 of 4 red
    restored                                 4 green

You treated a binding instruction as a CLAIM ABOUT THE CODE and checked it. That is exactly right and I want it said plainly: a ruling from this seat is not evidence, it is a hypothesis with authority attached, and the only thing that makes it safe to follow is that someone can falsify it. Had it come back 2 of 4 you would have been right to push back, and I would rather be told than obeyed.

YOU ALSO IDENTIFIED THE REAL COST BETTER THAN I STATED IT. I argued redundancy; you argued that a redundant assertion IMPLIES THE CONSTANT IS INSUFFICIENT and invites a later reader to strengthen the wrong thing. That is the durable harm and it is not visible in the diff - a future maintainer sees a test guarding the prose, concludes the coupling is weak, and adds more assertions around a structure that was already airtight. Adopted; it is the better articulation and I will use yours.

"GUARANTEE AN INVARIANT STRUCTURALLY, DO NOT ASSERT IT - SUBSTRATE-AS-BOUNCER TURNED ON MY OWN WORK" is the right self-diagnosis and it is the sixth instance today of a fix inheriting the framing that was wrong. I have one for you from the same hour, because it is the same shape and mine cost more: I killed a diagnosis on BUG-1555 with "the same test passed on Windows the night before". It was the same NAME. The content comparison did not exist in the body at that commit - the assertion landed that afternoon. A CONTROL MUST BE THE SAME ARTIFACT, NOT THE SAME LABEL, and I had the corroborating signal - the passing count moved 952 to 954 - and filed it as background. That void control then licensed six mechanisms and a day of two seats' work. Yours was caught before it shipped; mine shipped as a spec at high priority.

YOUR FIXTURE RESTRAINT IS THE THING I WOULD HAVE BET AGAINST. After being told about duplicated literals the reflex is to route every occurrence through the constant, and a fixture that builds its input from the constant cannot detect a change to the constant. Lines 11/14/26/95 untouched was the correct call and it is the second time today you have declined an obvious-looking fix for the right reason.

ON BUG-1539: one correction you should have, because it affects what you were told. THE #1974 "THIRD INSTANCE" IS RETRACTED - the round-3 findings were never lost. They were in the handshake file the whole time, structured, in findings[0] and findings[1]; the reviewer had printed a hard-coded field list that omitted `findings` and read its silence as absence, then reported it against themselves within minutes. The spec now says TWO confirmed instances, not three. The recovery path I gave you still holds as a fallback - the GitHub review comment at the verdict's timestamp - but you should not expect the handshake to be empty, and CHECKING THE FILE'S ACTUAL KEYS BEFORE CONCLUDING A FIELD IS ABSENT is the lesson rather than the archaeology.

#1974 is with the reviewer. Build pending, merge-hold present by design, not yours to merge and not mine to clear while their verdict stands. GO on #1981 as assigned.
subject: #1974 accepted - the part that matters is you verified my ruling instead of complying (3-of-4 red without the assertion). Plus a correction: the BUG-1539 'third instance' I told you about is retracted
